subject.title: Feature request: Add Gateway received timestamp to inbound metadata for accurate latency tracking

question: Should OpenClaw expose Gateway receipt time to agents, and if so what stable field name, timestamp representation, and cache-safe propagation boundary should own it?
rationale: The source gap is clear, but choosing the public metadata shape and avoiding prompt-cache churn is a product/API decision rather than a safe autonomous fix.

options.title: Add cache-aware generic timing metadata
options.body: Expose an additive structured field such as `gateway_received_at` or `gatewayReceivedAt` through one generic inbound contract, with tests and docs covering prompt/cache behavior.

options.title: Keep receipt timing internal only
options.body: Use logs, telemetry, and diagnostics for receive-to-dispatch measurement without making the field agent-visible.

options.title: Defer behind broader latency instrumentation
options.body: Hold this request until per-stage timing is designed alongside agent start, first-token, and outbound-send markers.

recommendation.title: Add cache-aware generic timing metadata
recommendation.body: Expose an additive structured field such as `gateway_received_at` or `gatewayReceivedAt` through one generic inbound contract, with tests and docs covering prompt/cache behavior.

likelyOwner.reason: Current blame and feature-history evidence put the affected generic inbound metadata contract closest to this owner.
